honorsAndAwards.title: The President's Scholar
honorsAndAwards.description: The President’s Scholar Program recognizes outstanding academic achievement by undergraduate students by providing a fifth year (i.e., a 9th and 10th terms) of study free of tuition. This benefit is intended to give students an opportunity to (1) pursue a second undergraduate degree, (2) pursue a graduate degree, or (3) undertake an advanced project of a scholarly or creative nature (e.g., a thesis, a portfolio of artwork, a design project, a field or laboratory research project) that does not lead to a degree. An overall GPA in Lehigh University graded coursework of at least a 3.75 at the time of application for the Scholarship. If the application is approved, the student must also have an overall GPA of 3.75 at the beginning of the Scholarship year.

honorsAndAwards.title: Dean's List
Eckardt Scholar
honorsAndAwards.description: The Eckardt Scholars Program is a highly selective and unique honors program in the College of Arts and Sciences. The program emphasizes deep intellectual curiosity, independent work, and close mentoring relationships between the very highest achieving students and faculty at Lehigh. Students in the program are exempt from the Arts & Sciences distribution requirements and work with their major advisor and the Eckardt Scholars Program Director to create a flexible course of study that best suits their academic interests and ambitions. Although exempt from Arts and Sciences distribution requirements, students will complete the requisite number of credits for their degrees and all correlative requirements for their departmental or interdisciplinary majors. The program includes participation in two Eckardt Scholar Seminars, and completion of a large independent project (in the form of a thesis, artistic creation, or other capstone experience) during the senior year.

headline: EY Digital Risk Principal and Americas Digital Compliance Solution Leader
about:
Brian Huston is a Principal in the Digital Risk practice of EY within the Chicago, IL office. He also serves as the Americas Digital Compliance Solution leader and EY’s HITRUST service offering leader. Brian specializes in cyber security, privacy, and regulatory compliance, specifically within the healthcare and technology sectors. Brian focuses on identifying, managing, and delivering high-quality consulting services, while also bringing relevant insights and industry experiences. 

Brian leads initiatives which helps organizations understand, mature, and establish cyber security and privacy capabilities that are effective and capable of withstanding external scrutiny (e.g., HITRUST certifications, ISO standard audits, CMMC (Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification) C3PAO audits, system and organization controls (SOC) reports, etc.). His efforts also support organizations to demonstrate compliance with regulations focused on the security and privacy of data (e.g., Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA), General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), etc.). Brian often advises teams on matters related to data privacy and regulatory compliance during merger and acquisition deals. Brian delivers pre-acquisition due diligence engagements for organizations including top private equity firms and Fortune 100 companies, focusing on data privacy and regulatory risks.

During the fall of 2015, Brian joined the Management Information System (MIS) Board of Advisors in the Eller College of Management at the University of Arizona. As part of the Board of Advisors, Brian is able to be a part of a team that helps move the MIS program with its three basic missions: educate students, conduct research, and engage in outreach activities.

about:
Before retiring, I led EY's National Tax Department. Prior to re-joining EY in 2011, I served at the US Treasury Department as the Assistant Secretary for Tax Policy, heading the Office of Tax Policy and advising Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner on all matters relating to taxation. Prior to my appointment as Assistant Secretary in 2009, I was the Deputy Assistant Treasury Secretary for International Tax Affairs. 

I began my career practicing tax law in 1993, at the New York law firm Sullivan & Cromwell, before moving to the Treasury Department, in 1997. I left the Treasury Department, in 2002, as the Deputy International Tax Counsel, and began working at EY, where I was a Partner in the International Tax Services group of EY’s National Tax Department, in Washington, DC, until 2007, when I returned to the Treasury Department.

I received my bachelor’s degree from Columbia University in 1986, my master's degree from the University of Chicago in 1988, my J.D. from the University of California Berkeley in 1992, and my LL.M. from the University of Miami in 1997. 

I have more than 20 years' experience in tax policy and tax planning, both in the private sector and the government. My specialties include global and US tax policy and international tax planning. I am based in Washington, DC.

I am a Manager in EY's Climate Change and Sustainability Services (CCaSS) practice with experience supporting a diverse range of clients on ESG strategy, measurement and reporting. With a background in finance, my approach to sustainability combines comprehensive, long-term business considerations and stakeholder engagement to develop ESG programs that drive returns and enhanced risk management alongside environmental and social impact.  

I have experience with all aspects of ESG program management, including developing sustainability strategies and performance improvement roadmaps, engaging and analyzing ESG rating agencies, performing materiality assessments, performing ESG risk assessments, identifying, measuring, and reporting environmental and social KPIs and targets (including GHG emission identification/scoping and calculation), development of ESG/sustainability reports, website disclosures and policies, and more. In addition, I have experience with emerging ESG frameworks, including the Task Force for Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), the World Economic Forum's Measuring Stakeholder Capitalism framework, and the World Resources Institute's Greenhouse Gas Protocol

about:
Jennifer is a trusted advisor focused on navigating complicated transaction and operational decisions.  To deliver meaningful advice, she draws upon a unique combination of modeling & analytics, investment banking, asset management and accounting experience to help clients accelerate growth and profitability.  Change is the environment of business today, and Jennifer embraces adaptive decision-making to build for the future. 

Currently, Jennifer applies her technical expertise in corporate finance and modeling to advise clients on the financial impact of major decisions, helping them to make more informed decisions.  Her specialty is a data-driven approach that generates value through forecasting, strategic options analysis, capital allocation, scenario planning, acquisition analysis, and post transaction consolidation models.

Previously, she had successfully executed an array of innovative transactions involving mergers & acquisitions (M&A), initial public offerings (IPOs), debt and equity follow-on offerings, and private placements.
